classification.difficultyReason: Select two Pythagorean subtriangles in the supplied kite, use diagonal bisection and combine segments before the standard area formula.

content.prompt: Find the lengths of the diagonals of this kite, and hence find its area.

spec.description: Complete actual source givens, perpendicular heights/equality families and mathematical shaded regions retained. Native editable black10pt figure, no derived dimensions.

answer.worked: The symmetry diagonal bisects the other, so that full diagonal is $2(12)=24$. Perpendicular right triangles give the two remaining segments $\sqrt{13^2-12^2}=5$ and $\sqrt{20^2-12^2}=16$. Hence the other full diagonal is $5+16=21$ and $A=\tfrac12(24)(21)=252$ square units.
